questions.question: What are antibiotics? Explain the difference between broad-spectrum and narrow-spectrum antibiotics and mention two common ones.
questions.solution:
**Antibiotics** are substances produced by microorganisms (or made synthetically) that inhibit the growth of, or destroy, other microorganisms.

**Broad-spectrum** antibiotics are effective against several classes of pathogens — e.g. tetracycline, chloramphenicol — but disturb the body's normal flora.

**Narrow-spectrum** ones act on a specific group — e.g. penicillin G (gram-positive bacteria) — and are preferred when the pathogen is known, giving fewer side effects.

They act by inhibiting cell-wall synthesis, protein synthesis or nucleic-acid function.
questions.knowledgeNote: Antibiotics are ineffective against viruses; overuse also selects resistant bacterial strains — the basis of antibiotic stewardship advice.

questions.question: Classify the following with an example each: (a) analgesic, (b) antacid, (c) antiseptic, (d) artificial sweetener — and state one misuse of drugs.
questions.solution:
**(a) Analgesic:** relieves pain — aspirin (also an anti-inflammatory and anticoagulant).

**(b) Antacid:** neutralises excess stomach acid — milk of magnesia, Mg(OH)₂ (the older NaHCO₃ causes CO₂ and acid rebound).

**(c) Antiseptic:** applied to living tissue to kill or prevent microbes — dettol, a mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol.

**(d) Artificial sweetener:** gives sweetness without calories — aspartame, ~100 times sweeter than sucrose (saccharin, 550 times).

**Misuse:** unrestricted use of barbiturates or amphetamines causes dependence; self-medicated antibiotics breed resistance.
questions.knowledgeNote: Antiseptics act on living tissue while disinfectants act on inanimate objects (0.2% phenol is antiseptic, 1% is disinfectant).

questions.question: What are detergents? Explain the cleansing action of soap and the reason soap forms scum with hard water.
questions.solution:
**Detergents** are sodium salts of long-chain sulphonic acids or alkyl sulphates; sodium soaps are salts of long-chain fatty acids.

**Cleansing action:** the molecule has a long hydrocarbon tail (soluble in grease) and a polar head (soluble in water). The tail dissolves in oily dirt while the head faces water, so micelles form with dirt at the centre, and the micelles are lifted from the fabric, emulsified and rinsed away.

**Scum:** soap anions combine with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ of hard water to give insoluble calcium/magnesium soaps (scum) that stick to fabric — detergents, whose calcium and magnesium salts are soluble, do not have this drawback.
questions.knowledgeNote: Detergents work in hard water and acidic solutions; soaps do not, because insoluble fatty-acid salts precipitate.
